Explanation: The Product Listing is the Core Value Unit in this marketplace boundary: a third-party Merchant's offer that can be discovered and purchased through JD's retail interface.

JD.com owns the retail platform and combines a large first-party retail operation with a third-party marketplace. This case isolates the marketplace layer while recognizing that its trust and logistics context comes from the wider JD system.
JD.com expands selection and monetization while preserving the quality expectations created by its controlled retail and supply-chain model.
Third-party supply broadens assortment and contributes marketplace and marketing revenue without JD owning all inventory.
JD must coordinate first-party retail, third-party Merchants, fulfillment choices and service quality without diluting customer trust.
JD coordinates marketplace discovery, ordering, payment and merchant settlement.
Transaction Flows: ← Consumer · Order / Pay — Shoppers place marketplace orders and pay through JD's commerce flow. | → Consumer · Match / Trust — JD provides discovery, transaction coordination and the trust context of its broader retail ecosystem. | ← Provider · Listing / Fees — Third-party Merchants provide listings and pay applicable marketplace or marketing fees. | → Provider · Demand / Payout — JD gives Merchants access to customer demand and coordinates order proceeds. | ← Partner · Services — External service partners contribute logistics, software, payments or other capabilities. | → Partner · Volume / Fees — JD's marketplace creates service volume and commercial relationships for enabling partners.
